Refactor into menu → level-select → per-level-scene architecture, and convert the block soup into a GridMap.

## 1. GridMap conversion (biggest change)

**MeshLibrary** — generated by `BakeLevel.cs` and saved to `res://assets/blocks.tres` with 4 items, each a unit cube BoxShape3D collision + mesh from existing `GameAssets`:
- 0: floor block (`block.glb` mesh, default material)
- 1: wall block (dark material)
- 2: beacon block (emissive cyan)
- 3: hollow block (`block_hollow.glb` wireframe)

**BakeLevel.cs rewrite** — same layout generation (disc floor, 3 rings, gates, beacons, high spans), but instead of thousands of StaticBody3D nodes it creates one `GridMap` (cell size 1,1,1) and `SetCellItem`s each block. Grid cell `(x, y, z)` maps from world `(i, 0.5 + k, j)` → cells `(i, k, j)` (y offset by -0.5 so floor is cell y=0). Output becomes `res://scenes/levels/level_1.tscn` (878KB → ~30KB).

**Level.cs rewrite** — wraps `GridMap` instead of scanning StaticBody3D children. Iterates `GridMap.GetUsedCells()` to build the sorted block list (Dist from cell world position). Block ops become `GridMap.SetCellItem(cell, HollowItem)` for hollowing and `SetCellItem(cell, -1)` for destruction — GridMap updates its collision automatically per cell change, so no QueueFree needed.

**Nothingness.cs** — unchanged logic, but hollow/destroy calls go through the new Level/GridMap API. Materials no longer overridden at runtime (hollow item carries the wireframe look).

## 2. Level scene contains everything

The baked `level_1.tscn` contains (as real saved nodes, not runtime-created):
- `LevelRoot` with `LevelRunner.cs` (refactored from Main.cs: game state, HUD labels, win/lose, R restart)
- WorldEnvironment + DirectionalLight3D (moved from Main.SetupWorld)
- `GridMap` (the level geometry)
- `Player` node (Player.cs script; still adds collision/mesh in _Ready)
- `CameraRig` (CameraRig.cs; change `Target` to `[Export]` so the tscn can wire it to Player)

Each level gets its own folder: `scenes/levels/level_1/level_1.tscn` + a short `level_1.md` description note (naming/radius/gates) so future levels follow the pattern.

## 3. Main menu + level select

**`scenes/main.tscn`** becomes the main menu (main_scene in project.godot unchanged): title "HOLLOW", Play and Quit buttons, built in code (matches existing style). Play → `ChangeSceneToFile("res://scenes/ui/level_select.tscn")`.

**`scenes/ui/level_select.tscn` + `LevelSelect.cs`** — scans `res://scenes/levels/*/​*.tscn` with `DirAccess` at runtime, shows one button per level (sorted), plus a Back button. All levels unlocked for now (progress system later). Clicking a level → `ChangeSceneToFile` that scene.

Small additions to LevelRunner: Esc returns to level select; win/lose screen gets "R retry · Esc levels".

## 4. File changes summary

- Rewrite: `BakeLevel.cs`, `Level.cs`, `Main.cs` → `scripts/ui/MainMenu.cs`, `Nothingness.cs` (block API only), `CameraRig.cs` (export Target)
- New: `scripts/ui/LevelSelect.cs`, `scripts/LevelRunner.cs`
- New scenes: `scenes/ui/level_select.tscn`, `scenes/levels/level_1/level_1.tscn` (baked)
- `scenes/main.tscn` rewritten as menu; delete old `scenes/level.tscn`, `assets/block_mesh.res`
- Run `dotnet build` + headless bake to verify output loads.

Note: no Blender MCP work needed this round — existing glb meshes are reused as MeshLibrary items.
